sources.title: MonoCode README.md
sources.finding: Desktop installers cover macOS, Linux and Windows. MonoCode uses existing coding-agent subscriptions; parallel tabs/worktrees, editing, diff review and /operator are documented. Production is React/Tauri, preview is Rust/GPUI.

sources.title: MonoCode docs/providers.md
sources.finding: Installed Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Pi and other named CLIs use their existing native logins. Missing providers are disabled individually with installation hints.

sources.title: MonoCode docs/agent-access.md
sources.finding: Opt-in /operator gives that active local thread a scoped app CLI. It starts, reads, sends, stops and organizes sessions/worktrees and notes with explicit IDs; uncertain writes retry with identical request IDs.

sources.title: MonoCode docs/remote-access.md
sources.locator: SSH setup; Sessions; Manage host; Scope
sources.finding: Remote Linux/macOS/Windows hosts run provider processes independently of the connecting desktop. SSH setup installs a host service and per-device credentials; remote files/Git/PRs work but operator, terminals and most local-only tools are unavailable.

sources.title: MonoCode mobile/README.md
sources.finding: The source-built Expo app uses QUIC/mTLS to show desktop projects, send prompts/start/stop turns and view changes. iOS/Android builds require native toolchains; approvals/questions remain on desktop, which must stay awake.

sources.title: MonoCode docs/native/parity.md
sources.finding: Preview is experimental, and source presence does not establish parity with production. Native automations/Monos and remote features retain documented verification gaps.

sources.title: MonoCode docs/native/preview-release-notes.md
sources.finding: Native preview release notes cover terminals, sessions, Git views and sign-in fixes; broad real-device parity is not established.

sources.title: MonoCode docs/jira.md
sources.finding: Jira Cloud inbox browses issues/comments, starts local work with ticket identity and polls issue-appeared automation. It supports unscoped API tokens, not Jira Data Center.

sources.title: MonoCode LICENSE
sources.finding: MonoCode repository code is MIT licensed, subject to provider names/logos and notices.

sources.title: MonoCode README
sources.finding: Says MonoCode works with your own Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other subscriptions and does not sell tokens. The license is MIT.
